evidence.title: In El Salvador’s mass trials, lawyers struggle to defend hundreds

occurrences.checkable_against: Salvadoran government statements defending mass trials
occurrences.quote_span: The Salvadoran government has defended the trials as necessary to dismantle gangs, given the scale of crime in the country.
occurrences.speaker: Salvadoran government
occurrences.subject: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials

occurrences.checkable_against: Human Rights Watch interview records
occurrences.quote_span: “Prosecutors say a person is a gang member because a police officer says so,” one lawyer anonymously told HRW.
occurrences.speaker: Anonymous defence lawyer
occurrences.subject: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials

occurrences.checkable_against: Human Rights Watch report and underlying criminal case files
occurrences.quote_span: HRW reported that, for the vast majority of prisoners convicted on such charges, the only evidence connecting them to a gang was a statement by one of two anonymous witnesses, who had received immunity from prosecution.
occurrences.speaker: Human Rights Watch
occurrences.subject: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials

occurrences.checkable_against: Al Jazeera correspondence records
occurrences.quote_span: The Salvadoran government did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials

occurrences.checkable_against: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials
occurrences.quote_span: The report, released on Wednesday, reviews four indictments covering more than 600 defendants and a single court ruling that involved more than 120 people.
occurrences.speaker: Human Rights Watch
occurrences.subject: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials

occurrences.checkable_against: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials
occurrences.quote_span: The report concludes that defendants in the mass trials face vaguely defined charges, weak evidence and faulty proceedings.
occurrences.speaker: Human Rights Watch
occurrences.subject: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials

occurrences.checkable_against: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials
occurrences.quote_span: The report, released on Wednesday, reviews four indictments covering more than 600 defendants and a single court ruling that involved more than 120 people.
occurrences.speaker: Human Rights Watch
occurrences.subject: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials

occurrences.checkable_against: Juanita Goebertus statement on El Salvador mass trials
occurrences.quote_span: “El Salvador’s mass trials are a mockery of justice,” said Juanita Goebertus, the Americas director at HRW, in a statement.
occurrences.speaker: Juanita Goebertus
occurrences.subject: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials

occurrences.checkable_against: Court ruling reviewed in Human Rights Watch report
occurrences.quote_span: In a single trial reviewed by the group, more than 120 people were convicted of unlawful association and sentenced to 30 or 45 years in prison.
occurrences.speaker: Human Rights Watch
occurrences.subject: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials

occurrences.checkable_against: International incarceration-rate statistics
occurrences.quote_span: The country has one of the highest incarceration rates in the world.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials

occurrences.checkable_against: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials
occurrences.quote_span: Human Rights Watch (HRW) has released a report documenting widespread violations as part of El Salvador’s mass trials, in which hundreds of people can be tried and convicted together.
occurrences.speaker: Human Rights Watch
occurrences.subject: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials

occurrences.checkable_against: El Salvador Tribunals Against Organized Crime records
occurrences.quote_span: The cases have been presented before the Tribunals Against Organized Crime, a court system overseen by El Salvador’s Supreme Court that critics accuse of a lack of transparency.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials

occurrences.checkable_against: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials
occurrences.quote_span: HRW noted that many convictions in the mass trials are secured by accusing the defendants of being “collaborators” with gangs, a vague legal standard.
occurrences.speaker: Human Rights Watch
occurrences.subject: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials

occurrences.checkable_against: Human Rights Watch interview records
occurrences.quote_span: “The prosecutor relies on the police report, and the police report relies on unspecified official intelligence or public rumours.”
occurrences.speaker: Anonymous defence lawyer
occurrences.subject: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials

occurrences.checkable_against: El Salvador prison population and population records
occurrences.quote_span: An estimated 120,000 people are currently imprisoned in El Salvador, equivalent to about 2 percent of the country’s population.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials

occurrences.checkable_against: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials
occurrences.quote_span: It also includes interviews with 15 defence lawyers, who say their clients were denied their due process rights and were therefore unable to adequately defend themselves at trial.
occurrences.speaker: Human Rights Watch
occurrences.subject: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials

occurrences.checkable_against: El Salvador prison population records
occurrences.quote_span: An estimated 120,000 people are currently imprisoned in El Salvador, equivalent to about 2 percent of the country’s population.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials

occurrences.checkable_against: Juanita Goebertus statement on El Salvador mass trials
occurrences.quote_span: “These hearings are designed to produce guilty verdicts, not to weigh evidence under due process.”
occurrences.speaker: Juanita Goebertus
occurrences.subject: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials

occurrences.checkable_against: Court ruling reviewed in Human Rights Watch report
occurrences.quote_span: No one was acquitted, HRW said.
occurrences.speaker: Human Rights Watch
occurrences.subject: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials

occurrences.checkable_against: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials
occurrences.quote_span: In its report, HRW called for independent reviews of cases brought under the state of emergency.
occurrences.speaker: Human Rights Watch
occurrences.subject: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials

occurrences.checkable_against: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials
occurrences.quote_span: It also demanded that people detained without credible evidence be released.
occurrences.speaker: Human Rights Watch
occurrences.subject: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials

occurrences.checkable_against: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials
occurrences.quote_span: In some cases, defence lawyers have reportedly been restricted from viewing their clients’ case files and communicating privately with the defendants.
occurrences.speaker: Human Rights Watch
occurrences.subject: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials

occurrences.checkable_against: Tribunals Against Organized Crime judge disclosure records
occurrences.quote_span: The identities of the tribunals’ judges have not been disclosed, even to the lawyers involved in the proceedings.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials

occurrences.checkable_against: El Salvador government records on security crackdown
occurrences.quote_span: The mass trials are part of President Nayib Bukele’s sweeping security crackdown, launched in response to a surge in organised crime in the country.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Human Rights Watch report on El Salvador mass trials
